chunks: Aḥmad ibn Mihrān, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Abū ʿAlī al-Khazzāz, from Dāwūd ibn Sulaymān, who said:

I said to Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام: “Indeed, I fear that some event may occur and I may not meet you, so inform me who the Imam is after you.” So he said: “My son, so-and-so,” meaning Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام.

key_terms.أَبَا الْحَسَنِ: Abū al-Ḥasan, the intended successor mentioned in the report
key_terms.أَبِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Abū Ibrāhīm, the Imam being addressed in this narration
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the divinely designated leader after the previous Imam
key_terms.بَعْدَكَ: after you, referring to succession following the Imam

ai.seo_question: How did Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام indicate the Imam after him?
ai.summary: This hadith records a direct designation by Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام of the Imam after him. It highlights the continuity of the Imamate through explicit indication and identifies Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام as his successor.
